activities.anchor: jobs-to-be-done framing states the underlying need rather than the stated solution
activities.caption: walk the OXO strategy decision
activities.name: stratOxoBranch

config.root: A metal peeler is hard for a hand with arthritis to use. Walk the strategy that answered it.

choices.label: Contextual inquiry in real kitchens — grip strength, wet surfaces, pressure
choices.feedback: Context decides requirements that no feature list can — the research discipline run upstream, funded as strategy.

choices.label: A satisfaction survey about peelers
choices.feedback: People are unreliable narrators of their own behaviour — and designing for the demo room instead of the kitchen is discovered in returns data.

frame.text: The findings are in. What is the strategy?

choices.label: One decision — the most comfortable handle anyone has held
choices.feedback: A handle that works for a 5th-percentile hand and a 95th turned one gadget into a category-defining line.

choices.label: A better peeler for arthritis sufferers
choices.feedback: The diagnosis framing caps the market and misses the mechanism — the context, not the condition, decides the design.

done.text: Pressure, grip, the wet kitchen: one context-of-use decision that comforted everyone and widened the funnel.

survey.text: Strategy failures are symmetrical: wrong context, wished-for user — both found in the returns data, too late.

niche.text: Design for the user the company wishes it had, or the user the category expects — and the strategy stays small.

config.why: The strategist's skill is converting user needs and context of use into investment decisions — not into per-project features.

activities.anchor: the classic demonstration being the 1950s US Air Force cockpit study
activities.caption: one-size vs the neutral grip — drag the divider
activities.name: stratGripCompare

config.prompt: The handle decision, two ways — drag between them:

before.label: One-size tool handle
before.text: Excludes small and large hands simultaneously and invites strain injuries — a musculoskeletal-disorder cost that lands on someone's insurance.

after.label: Geometrically neutral grip
after.text: Comfortable for hands at both ends of the distribution — widens the market and reduces harm with one decision.

config.why: Ergonomics is where design's ethical and commercial interests most cleanly align — which is why it deserves a seat in the strategy.

activities.anchor: on any realistic bundle of dimensions, almost nobody is average
activities.caption: true or false — the average user
activities.name: stratAverageJudge

statements.s: There is a typical user whose measurements represent everyone.
statements.why: Measured across enough human measurements at once, the middle of every one is a near-empty set.

statements.s: Adjustable ranges across the population are the fit mechanism.
statements.why: The cockpit fix, generalised into a standing fit policy.

statements.s: Who sits in the tails of the distribution is a deliberate decision.
statements.why: Gloves, clothing allowance, children versus adults — the context decision returns.

statements.s: Percentile design is purely an ethics play that costs market reach.
statements.why: The neutral grip widened the market and reduced harm with one decision — ethics and commerce aligned.

activities.anchor: captions serve deaf and loud-pub viewers alike
activities.caption: pair each brand force with its mechanism
activities.name: stratForceMatch

config.prompt: Three forces the market reads at a glance — pair each:

pairs.right: the aesthetic-usability effect — attractive interfaces are perceived as working better
legal force plus a trust asset — standards, hazard analysis, CE marking
the curb-cut effect — features built for one group improve it for everyone
one design language recognisable across a thousand SKUs

config.why: In the market the three compound: quality signalled, trust sustained, the funnel widened — each measurable, each a leadership commitment.

activities.anchor: because project-by-project sustainability enthusiasm reliably reaches for the easiest R
activities.caption: sequence the six-R hierarchy
activities.name: stratSixROrder

config.prompt: The order is the strategy — sequence the six Rs:
items: Rethink — does this product need to exist?
Reduce — material and energy intensity per function
Repair — fixability as a designed property
Recycle — deliberately last: infrastructure outside the designer's control
config.why: Rethink and Refuse act at design time and dwarf everything downstream; Recycle recovers only a fraction of embodied value — the easiest R is the weakest one.

activities.anchor: the honest line between appreciation and appropriation is research plus collaboration
activities.caption: find the faulty line — the contextual audit
activities.name: stratCultureSpot

config.prompt: One of these context claims is backwards — click it:
lines: The precedent audit analyses prior solutions — teardowns, patents, the canon.
Innovation that ignores precedent usually rediscovers its failures.
Trend cycles are real market forces; chasing every one forfeits recognisability.
Colour symbolism is universal, so palettes travel untouched across markets.
Reading direction flips layouts — Arabic runs right-to-left.
config.correction: Colour meaning varies: white is bridal in Europe and mourning in parts of East Asia — cultural context decides meaning.
config.why: The costliest design failures are context failures — entirely preventable with research that costs a rounding error.

activities.anchor: Conway's law — the org chart ships in the product
activities.caption: fill the blanks — the quantitative evidence
activities.name: stratEvidenceCloze

config.text: McKinsey's Design Index found top-quartile design organisations delivered roughly %%0%% percentage points higher revenue growth, and the Design Value Index tracked design-led firms beating the S&P 500 by more than %%1%% percent across a decade — correlational, caveated, but directionally consistent. The toolkit converts evidence into capability: principles as %%2%% filters, research funded as infrastructure, and metrics owned jointly with product.
config.hint: Two big numbers from two independent studies, and the small instrument that settles debates.

activities.anchor: high-contrast interfaces serve sunlight and ageing eyes alike
activities.caption: charity or option value? drag the divider
activities.name: stratCurbCompare

config.prompt: Two readings of inclusive design — drag between them:

before.label: The charity reading
before.text: Accommodations added for a small minority, budgeted against the roadmap — a cost centre to minimise.

after.label: The curb-cut reading
after.text: Kerb ramps ended up serving prams, luggage and delivery trolleys; subtitles serve bars, language learners and noisy trains — designing for the edges routinely upgrades the centre.

config.why: Inclusivity is option value built into the roadmap — a practice that widens the funnel, not charity budgeted against it.
